collection_metadata.locality: Pitchandikulam Forest, Auroville, Tamil Nadu, India

stem_bark.text: The bark of Spondias pinnata is light-brown or greyish-coloured. It is smooth and becomes deeply cracked on old individuals.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Spondias pinnata is light-brown or greyish-coloured. It is smooth and becomes deeply cracked on old individuals.

seed.text: The seed of Spondias pinnata is enclosed in a big stone. The stone is ellipsoid, 3-3.5 cm long and 2 mm wide.
seed.text_html: The seed of Spondias pinnata is enclosed in a big stone. The stone is ellipsoid, 3-3.5 cm long and 2 mm wide.

ecology.text: Spondias pinnata is found in dry to moist deciduous forests from the coastal plains up to 1000 m of elevation.
ecology.text_html:
• Ecology :

    Spondias pinnata is found in dry to moist deciduous forests from the coastal plains up to 1000 m of elevation.

distribution.text: Tropical areas of Africa, Asia and Oceania (excluding Australia and New Zealand)
distribution.text_html:
• Distribution :

    Tropical areas of Africa, Asia and Oceania (excluding Australia and New Zealand)

reproduction_dispersal.text: Spondias pinnata is polygamous : it has male, female, and bisexual flowers on the same plant. Spondias pinnata is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. The seeds of Spondias pinnata are dispersed by various fruit-eating birds and mammals.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Spondias pinnata is polygamous : it has male, female, and bisexual flowers on the same plant.

  • Mode of pollination :

    Spondias pinnata is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Spondias pinnata are dispersed by various fruit-eating birds and mammals.

culinary.text: The raw or cooked fruit of Spondias pinnata is edible. It can be eaten as a vegetable or made into chutneys, stews, pickles and jams. Source : Plant Resources of Southeast Asia, http://proseanet.org

medicinal.text: Spondias pinnata is used in Ayurveda, Unani and Siddha medicines. The bark of Spondias pinnata is used in dysentery, diarrhea, biliousness, menstrual disorders, arthritis, tuberculosis, for rubbing on the skin over painful joints. The bark paste is used for stomach and body pain. The bark paste is applied externally to articular and muscular rheumatism. The bark juice is taken for diarrhea and dysentery and also applied on ringworm and skin diseases. The leaves juice is dropped in the ear in earache. The fruit is used as an astringent, blood purifier, antiscorbutic and against dyspepsia. The fruit juice is applied or dropped against earache and also taken to stop blood dysentery. The root is used for regulating menstruation. Sources : - Khare, 2007, Indian Medicinal Plants, An Illustrated Dictionary - Quattrocchi, 2012, CRC World Dictionary of Medicinal and Poisonous Plants
medicinal.text_html:
Spondias pinnata is used in Ayurveda, Unani and Siddha medicines.

The bark of Spondias pinnata is used in dysentery, diarrhea, biliousness, menstrual disorders, arthritis, tuberculosis, for rubbing on the skin over painful joints.
The bark paste is used for stomach and body pain.
The bark paste is applied externally to articular and muscular rheumatism.
The bark juice is taken for diarrhea and dysentery and also applied on ringworm and skin diseases.

The leaves juice is dropped in the ear in earache.

The fruit is used as an astringent, blood purifier, antiscorbutic and against dyspepsia.
The fruit juice is applied or dropped against earache and also taken to stop blood dysentery.

The root is used for regulating menstruation.

Sources :
- Khare, 2007, Indian Medicinal Plants, An Illustrated Dictionary
- Quattrocchi, 2012, CRC World Dictionary of Medicinal and Poisonous Plants

reforestation.text: Spondias pinnata is able to flourish in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. It thrives in open areas. Spondias pinnata requires a sunny position in a well-drained soil. The species is propagated by seeds. 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Spondias pinnata is able to flourish in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. It thrives in open areas.
    Spondias pinnata requires a sunny position in a well-drained soil.
    The species is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
